description: Construction rule for a public trust receipt. This is an ALLOWLIST, not a denylist: a canonical receipt field absent from disclosableFields is excluded, so an internal field added later cannot leak by default. This file is data, not documentation - the conformance test reads it rather than trusting prose.

withheldFields.workspaceId: tenancy identifier; reveals whose receipt this is
withheldFields.admissionId: internal correlation id, joinable across receipts
withheldFields.memoryDraftId: internal correlation id, joinable across receipts
withheldFields.provenanceId: internal correlation id, joinable across receipts
withheldFields.approvalId: internal correlation id, joinable across receipts
withheldFields.reason: free text written by the runtime; unbounded content
withheldFields.metadata: arbitrary object; the highest-risk field by construction
withheldFields.schemaVersion: internal format marker; the public receipt declares its own
withheldFields.previousReceiptHash: chain position; disclosing it would let a holder walk the internal chain
withheldFields.receiptHash: carried in binding.internalReceiptHash instead, where its role is explicit

receiptIdDecision.justification: The authorization pack required this choice to be made explicitly rather than silently. A stable identifier is correlatable across disclosures: two public receipts derived from the same internal receipt carry the same publicReceiptId. That is accepted here because binding.internalReceiptHash is ALREADY a stable correlator and is mandatory - a recipient needs it to check the receipt against a bundle they hold. Claiming unlinkability while shipping that hash would be incoherent. So this format does not offer unlinkability, and says so, rather than offering a weak version of it. A per-disclosure salted identifier would break the recipient's ability to recognise the same receipt twice and would still not deliver unlinkability while binding remains mandatory.

integrity.checksumInput: the public receipt with integrity.checksum removed, serialized by the canonicalJson rule of the source above
integrity.signatureNote: No signing implementation exists: lib/v5/verification-core.js accepts only algorithm test-structural-v1 and synthetic-signature-placeholder values, which issue #435 is open against.

assuranceLevels.checksum: corruption and self-consistency detection. Keyless, so an editor who rewrites the document can recompute it. It does not prove the document was not altered.
assuranceLevels.signature: issuer and authorship. Not delivered by this format today.
assuranceLevels.externalHashComparison: independently anchored evidence: comparing binding.internalReceiptHash or binding.bundleHash against a receipt or bundle the recipient obtained separately. This is the only level here that survives a capable editor.

integrity.signedSignatureCoupling: signed false requires signature null; signed true requires an ed25519-v1 signature object. Enforced by oneOf in the schema, not by convention.
